artifacts.review-report:
# AC3d independent review (architecture, ownership and requirement trace)

Scope: uncommitted snapshot over baseline 9bb84c6. I read src/ergora/workflow_definitions.py, src/ergora/definition_bundles.py, src/ergora/agent_definitions.py, src/ergora/backups.py, src/ergora/cli.py (composition branch and error handling), src/ergora/contracts.py, src/ergora/data/schemas/workflow-definition-v1.json, tests/test_workflow_definitions.py, the tests/test_agent_definitions.py diff, examples/composition (README, kernel-delivery and parallel-review workflow.json, preview-grant.json), docs/WORKFLOW_DEFINITIONS.md, ADR0005 and the delivery record. Logs read: r1-source-tests.log (135 passed/2 skipped), r1-expanded-source-tests.log and r1-wheel-tests.log (each 177 passed/8 skipped, 1 FastAPI deprecation warning), r1-build.log, package-identities.json and r1-cli-journey.json. I ran no commands and modified nothing. Logs are treated as evidence, not verdicts.

## Blocking findings
None.

## Requirement trace (all reached through real call paths)
- Immutable versioned packages with exact references: node refs carry kind, id, version and whole-bundle digest. _Compilation._resolve (workflow_definitions.py:143-151) re-checks the digest against the library entry. DefinitionLibrary.import_bundle (definition_bundles.py:127-162) refuses same-version/different-content, refuses to replace missing registered objects, and publishes the index last. Tests cover missing-ref, digest and same-version cases.
- Bounded static DAG, named ports, all-join: _levels uses a TopologicalSorter, which also rejects self-dependency. _links requires every input binding to be a workflow input or a direct dependency's declared output. A join waits on every listed branch. Reference cycles are impossible because refs are digest-pinned; the lineage check is belt-and-braces.
- Stable independent paths: paths are built from kebab node ids, and repeated refs yield distinct instances and distinct prompt SHAs (test_repeated_references...).
- Full ancestor accumulation: _materials deep-copies the inherited list per child, so siblings and predecessors never leak in. Order is root to leaf and the leaf's own resources come last. Dedup preserves every logical id and every source. Logical-id conflicts with different kind or content are rejected. Loading-name conflicts are checked by frontmatter skill name, not logical id (workflow_definitions.py:101-123).
- Narrowing cannot discard inherited material: _readable checks every source URI of every merged resource against the instance's read scope, including after dedup. The test with a narrowed read scope fails with 'Required inherited resource is not readable'.
- Permissions: _within is applied at root against the grant, at each workflow against its parent, and at each agent node against its workflow, so the check is transitive. Network origins are canonical origins with the port range checked at parse time. Write is workspace-only. Path matching is by segment, not string prefix. A joint parent/child raise through new pinned versions works, the old root's preview stays identical, and a child-only raise fails.
- Caps: every structural instance, including root and joins, is counted in every enclosing scope plus the project scope. Depth is measured per scope and globally, and material bytes are charged per leaf prompt to every active scope. Concurrency is reported per scope in the leaf preview. That matches the documented static-preview contract; enforcement belongs to AC4d.
- No scripts or model calls on import: the import path only reads files and hashes. check and failed-preview paths create no State (tested through the real CLI).
- Backup/restore: backups._check_assets now calls workflow_definitions.verify_store, which re-previews every stored workflow against the Agent library under the backup data root. The test shows a self-consistent forged object and index still fail with 'reference digest mismatch'. Pre-AC3d backups without the directory verify as 0.
- Legacy contracts: agent_definitions keeps its public signatures. Storage directory, lock file name, temp prefixes, index schema and return shapes match the removed code in the diff. My grep found no remaining consumers of the removed private helpers in src or tests. asset_trees is untouched, the workflow CLI stays legacy forwarding, and package-identities.json reports 283 frozen files PASS. The wheel-installed hashes for cli, backups, contracts, agent_definitions, definition_bundles, workflow_definitions and the new schema equal the protected manifest.
- Preview is explicitly executable=false and lists three pending runtime checks. No second scheduler was introduced.

## Architecture assessment
Dependency direction is acyclic: workflow_definitions -> agent_definitions -> definition_bundles -> asset_trees/skill_assets/contracts. definition_bundles owns package inspection and immutable publication. Both libraries inject only their semantic inspector, which is a real second implementation rather than a test-only seam. Graph, permission and budget semantics stay in the workflow owner. The compiler is one cohesive class and is rightly not split further.

## Non-blocking suggestions (optional, none gate approval)
S1. docs/architecture/decisions/0005-composable-workflows.md:3 still says 'design proposal, not yet implemented', while docs/architecture/current.md and the delivery record say the static part is implemented by AC3d. Add a status line scoped to the static AC3d part. A reader trusting the ADR header would misjudge shipped scope.
S2. src/ergora/workflow_definitions.py:263-273 builds a DefinitionLibrary inline, duplicating the constructor in library() (lines 82-83). Giving library() an optional inspector argument removes the duplication. Separately, verify_store re-previews every stored workflow, so children are re-expanded under each parent. Correct, and bounded by the 512-instance cap, but superlinear in library size. No measurement was supplied, so I make no performance claim.
S3. definition_bundles.read_json now says 'Definition content changed while reading' where the old Agent code said 'Agent content changed while reading'. No test pins it and the behaviour is the same, but it is a small drift in an existing public message.
S4. Same-loading-name/different-tree conflict between two Skill resources inside one bundle is caught by the same _materials loop at import, but no test covers it and check does not report it, since check is local-only by design. Consider one test.
S5. examples/composition/preview-grant.json grants write:[workspace] and shell:true. The manual already says operators should narrow it; consider a read-only default example.
S6. A child limit larger than its ancestor's, for example concurrency, is not rejected statically. The effective limit is the minimum across the listed scopes. This is acceptable for a static preview, but make sure AC4d enforces the minimum.

## Evidence notes
- r1-build.log shows a failed build attempt (Unmet dependencies: wheel not installed) in the older ac3a-definitions venv. I did not see a successful build log. The wheel identity rests on package-identities.json (wheel_sha256, installed file hashes matching the manifest, 283 frozen files, verify PASS, 359 installed files). Record the successful build command and log in the WD5 delivery record.
- The delivery record still cites 135/2. Add the 177/8 source and wheel results and the 26-command CLI journey (10 instances, backup manifest SHA recorded) when WD5 closes.
- 8 skips cover native Windows junction handling and the fixed-SDK cases. They do not prove those operations; do not cite them as such.
- Different harness from the author (Claude vs Codex) reduces shared-harness bias but does not prove statistical independence.
- This was a static source review. I did not re-run the tests or the CLI journey, and I did not independently rebuild the wheel.

summary: Approve. The AC3d static package, library and preview slice meets the raw requirements within the stated static-only scope. I found no blocking defect. Non-blocking suggestions and evidence-record notes are listed separately in the report.
